findings.issue: Vite's import.meta.glob() gets round both new allow-lists and the headless ban on dynamic import(). HEADLESS_RESTRICTED_SYNTAX bans only ImportExpression. import.meta.glob is a MetaProperty member call, so neither no-restricted-imports nor the TSImportType selectors see it. Vite rewrites it into real imports (static imports with { eager: true }) of any matching project module. tsconfig includes the vite/client types, so it typechecks. Vitest supports it too. A bot or advice file can then load src/storage/hand-store (sharedHandStore -> stored records with replay codes) or src/table/session (TableState.hand, botTurn) at runtime. That is the round-1 MAJOR path again, one syntax away. It is also an idiomatic Vite feature (e.g. for loading styles/*.json), so it could turn up without anyone meaning harm.
findings.evidence: Linted in-process with the repo config: src/bots/zz.ts `export const m = import.meta.glob('../storage/*.ts', { eager: true });` -> 0 errors; the same in src/advice/zz.ts -> 0 errors. No headless module uses import.meta today (grep of src/engine, bots, advice, stats, playtest, table), so a ban breaks nothing.
findings.fix: Add { selector: "MetaProperty[meta.name='import'][property.name='meta']", message: 'import.meta (including import.meta.glob) is not allowed in headless modules (REQ-059.2).' } to HEADLESS_RESTRICTED_SYNTAX. It flows into the bot and advice blocks through BOT_DETERMINISM_RESTRICTED_SYNTAX. Add a probe for src/bots and one for src/advice to the acceptance test.

findings.issue: Bot and advice code can still reach IndexedDB, and so the stored past hands with their replay codes, without importing anything. no-restricted-properties matches only static property names. BARE_GLOBAL_REFERENCE exempts any `globalThis` that is the object of a member expression, including computed ones. eval, indirect eval and the Function constructor are not banned either. This was already missing before this change, and it takes deliberate evasion rather than drift, so it is defence in depth.
findings.evidence: src/bots/zz.ts: `globalThis['indexed' + 'DB']`, `const k = 'indexedDB'; globalThis[k]`, `(0, eval)('indexedDB')`, `new Function('return indexedDB')()` and `Function('return this')()` each -> 0 lint errors. The same holds in src/advice. Window, self and Worker are already blocked (no-restricted-globals).
findings.fix: In the headless (or bot-determinism) syntax list add { selector: "MemberExpression[computed=true][object.name='globalThis']" }, and enable 'no-eval', 'no-implied-eval' and 'no-new-func' for HEADLESS_FILES (or at least src/bots/** and src/advice/**). Bare `Function` could go in BARE_GLOBAL_REFERENCE's name list.

summary: Round-1 MAJORs are fixed. Both boundaries are now allow-lists. Checked in-process with the repo config, all of these are blocked in src/bots: ../storage/hand-store, ../table/session (type-only, inline type, type namespace, value namespace, export *, export type *, export * as), TableState/BotTurn through TSImportType including indexed access and typeof import, import x = require (value and type), plain require, Worker, non-normalized and query-string paths, ../engine/. and advice/golden (case-insensitive). In src/advice: storage, table re-exports, ./golden and ./Golden re-exports, engine/hand namespace and export *, HandState in type position, ./charts/../../ traversal and the playerView value. Round-1 MINORs (golden extension/type-position bypass, advice re-exporting golden) and the NIT (advice type-position HandState) are also fixed. The advice sibling closure holds: every src/advice file except golden.ts is under the same block, and the five allowed engine modules import only ./cards. No module puts the hand store or table state on globalThis. What remains: (MAJOR) import.meta.glob gets round every import rule and is a runtime path to storage/hand-store and table/session from bot and advice code. (MINOR, already missing before this change) computed globalThis access and eval/Function reach indexedDB directly. No new dependencies, secrets or randomness changes.
